history.install: {kind} isn't on this computer yet. Puppet Master installs it while your Project is created.
history.keeps: This folder already keeps its versions with {kind}, so Puppet Master keeps using it.
history.detail: Four things keep your work safe, and each has its own job. Safe History keeps earlier versions of your Project on this computer, so you can go back to one. FileSafe guards your files while the AI works. An online copy keeps your Project on a website such as GitHub. A backup is a separate copy somewhere else, for when this computer is lost. Without an online copy or a backup, your Project is only on this computer.
history.detailExpert: Safe History is local version control, Git or Jujutsu, in the Project folder: no account, no remote. Jujutsu runs colocated with a Git repository, so any Git remote works with either. FileSafe is the agent guard layer: command blocklist, write scope, security filter, pre-write safe points. The online copy is a remote repository on the service you choose. The backup is an encrypted, independent repository at a destination you choose, restored with the Recovery Kit. Without a remote or a backup, the only copy is local.

fail.refused: {name} refused the key because its home folder is shared too widely.
fail.not_allowed: This account isn't allowed to use SSH on {name}.

notAllowedBy.Synology: Synology lets only accounts in its administrators group use SSH. Sign in with such an account, or use a shared folder instead.
notAllowedBy.QNAP: On QNAP, who may use SSH is set in Control Panel › Network & File Services › Telnet / SSH › Edit Access Permission. Or use a shared folder instead.
notAllowedBy.TrueNAS: On TrueNAS, the account has to be allowed to sign in over SSH: Credentials › Users › Edit. Or use a shared folder instead.
notAllowedBy.Unraid: Unraid lets only its root account use SSH. Sign in as root, or use a shared folder instead.

three_outcomes.title: The idea becomes three clear outcomes.

review.title: Review before anything is built.
review.after: Nothing has been built yet. This is your chance to check the outcome, the decisions Puppet Master used, and anything that is still uncertain.

review_parts.title: Read the plan before anything is built.
review_parts.part1: Outcomes: what the finished website must do for the people who use it.
review_parts.part2: Decisions: the choices your answers made. Change an answer and these change with it.
review_parts.part3: Assumptions: what Puppet Master takes for granted. Say so if one is wrong.
review_parts.part4: Still open: anything you have not decided yet. Puppet Master does not guess.
review_parts.do: Outcomes, decisions, assumptions and what is still open: read these before you let any work begin.
review_parts.doEli5: That is the whole plan. Read it before work begins.

answer_edit.title: Plans change when answers change.
answer_edit.do: Change your answer and watch what moves.

consequence_changed.title: Only the affected parts changed.
consequence_changed.do: Everything else kept its place, so you can see cause and effect.

completion_boundary.title: You decide when work begins.
completion_boundary.do: That is the planning loop: describe the outcome, answer only the questions that matter, review the plan, then decide whether to begin.
completion_boundary.doEli5: Describe it, answer, review, then decide.

teacher.label: Guided example · Teacher
teacher.popover: Written in advance for the Guided Tour. It doesn’t use your AI plan.
teacher.q1: What happens before Puppet Master changes my files?
teacher.a1: Before work begins, Puppet Master turns your request into a plan. You can review the important choices, correct anything that looks wrong, and decide when to begin. Your Project permissions still control what the work may change.
teacher.a1eli5: First, Puppet Master writes down what it thinks you want. You can fix the plan before anything starts. It waits for your decision to begin.
teacher.a2: A Project keeps one body of work—its files, plans, history, and Project-specific settings—together.
teacher.a2eli5: A Project is one workspace for one thing you are making. It keeps the right files and decisions together.
teacher.explainDetail: Adds one simpler reply under this one. The reply itself and this chat’s ELI5 stay as they are.
teacher.explains: Simpler explanation of the reply above
teacher.own: Teacher answers tour questions from its guide. Try one of these:

endpoint.spaces: An address has no spaces in it.
endpoint.scheme: Use an address that starts with https:// so the connection is protected.
endpoint.credentials: Leave out any user name or password. You sign in after connecting.
endpoint.port: The number after the colon has to be between 1 and 65535.
endpoint.host: That doesn't look like an address yet. It should look like pm.example.com.
endpoint.hostname: Use a name, like pm.example.com, not a number. The web address needs a name of its own.
endpoint.path: Use the address on its own, like https://pm.example.com, with nothing after it. Puppet Master needs a whole web address of its own.
endpoint.query: Leave out anything after a ? or a #.
endpoint.short: That's too short for a Remote Link or its code.
endpoint.long: That's too long for a Remote Link or its code.
